idea-plugin.name: Maven Prime
idea-plugin.description:
Everything you expect from a Maven plugin, plus the answers none of them give you. Run and debug any goal, run your tests the way Maven runs them, win any dependency argument. Then find out why the build is slow, where a version really came from, and what is rotting in your local repository.

  • Goals you save once, each one a real IDE action with its own shortcut.
  • Tests run and debugged through Maven, reported in the IDE test tree.
  • Dependency Analyzer on the tree the IDE already resolved: conflicts, every path, and why.
  • Effective values inline: every ${property} and inherited version, in the POM.
  • Profiler: the critical path of a parallel build, and whether raising -T helps.
  • Model: every version, plugin and property beside the POM that really set it.
  • Repository: what is missing, half-downloaded or negatively cached in ~/.m2.
  • Build context shared with your team, with your own machine always winning.
  • Maven Daemon found or installed for you, and options rendered for Maven 3, 4 or mvnd.

Run and debug any goal, on the module you are already in

One popup, from the editor or the project tree, already pointed at the right module. Save the goals you keep retyping: each one becomes a real IDE action, so it gets its own keyboard shortcut and its own toolbar button. A saved goal carries its own profiles, properties, options, JRE and Maven version, so the fast build and the thorough one live side by side.

  • Run icons in the gutter of pom.xml: the whole module, one plugin, one execution.
  • Run a goal before any run configuration launches, as a before-launch step.
  • Force Clean, skip tests and offline are toggles, not edits to the goals you saved.
  • Colored Maven output. Maven gives up on color inside an IDE; Maven Prime asks for it anyway.

Run and debug your tests through Maven

Run one test method or one test class the way Maven will run it in CI, and read the result in the IDE test tree instead of scrolling console output. Debug attaches to the JVMs that Surefire forks, so a breakpoint inside the test is actually hit.

Win the dependency argument

The analyzer opens on the pom.xml you are reading, in the editor, on the tree the IDE has already resolved, so there is nothing to wait for. It shows which versions clashed, which one won, and every path that drags an artifact in.

  • Every path also says why it was kept or dropped: omitted for conflict, managed by dependency management, duplicate, excluded. Seeing the paths is not the same as knowing the reason.
  • Exclude the one you do not want and Maven Prime writes it into the declaration that actually causes it. When that declaration is inherited, it tells you where, instead of quietly changing every module that inherits it.
  • Jump from any artifact straight into your local repository, and back again.
  • Sort by size on disk, when you need to know what made the build heavy.

That is the part you already expect. Here is the rest.

Know why the build is slow

Per-module times tell you nothing about a parallel build. Maven Prime measures the build from the inside, lays it out as a timeline with one lane per module that really ran at the same time, and gives you the one answer you actually wanted: raise -T to this and save that much, or stop trying, because these modules are the critical path.

Every ${property} resolved, in the POM you are reading

A placeholder shows what the effective model actually resolved it to, right beside it, and not only inside a version tag. A dependency or plugin with no version shows the one it inherits from dependency or plugin management. Click a value and the file that decided it opens on the line, parent POMs included. No build to run, no tab to open, no guessing which ancestor won.

Know where a version came from

Every dependency, every plugin and every property, beside the POM that really set it. Parents included, even the ones that exist only in your local repository. One double-click and you are looking at the line.

One build context, honored everywhere

Profiles, properties and the Maven environment in one place, applied to every run. Flip a profile and the effective model reloads itself, so what the IDE resolves is what your next build will really do.

Keep that context in the repository and the whole team has it on the next pull. Your own changes always win, so a shared setup never fights your machine, and nothing from a repository applies until you trust it.

A local repository you can trust

Artifacts that were never downloaded, that answered 404 everywhere, or that died halfway. Which repositories were tried, and when. Sources and javadoc that are not really there. And when Maven has cached a failure and refuses to retry, clear it for that one artifact instead of deleting your local repository and downloading the internet again.

  • Any artifact in your local repository, straight from Search Everywhere.
  • Newer published versions show up on their own: no button, no request, no waiting.
  • Credentials for the repository that refused you, kept in the IDE password safe.

Builds that start instantly

The Maven Daemon keeps the JVM warm between builds. Maven Prime finds the one you have or installs one for you, keeps the daemons in check, and never sends an option the Maven you picked cannot run: it drops it and tells you which one.

And the small things you keep wishing for

  • Add as Dependency writes the element into the module POM for you.
  • Any dependency copied as ready-to-paste XML, or as plain coordinates.
  • Intentions on the POM: analyze an artifact, go to the version that decided it, exclude it.
  • Options rendered for the Maven that will really run it, whether that is Maven 3, Maven 4 or mvnd.
  • The recent builds are kept, not only the last one, so the run that failed differently is one pick away instead of another rerun.
  • The goals you save and the whole build context travel in one file at the root of the repository.
